title: We Lost Our Tire Deal Two Days Before the Race | Club Karting Ep. 14
creator: Pit Lane Pals
description:
Round 5 of the regional club championship. Used tires, a rain shower, and Danny's best qualifying of the season.

Team: Danny (driver), Mo (mechanic), Bex (camera and everything else)
Track: Riverside Kart Circuit

Episode 13: last week's crash and rebuild

Instagram: @pitlanepals

sentences.t: Okay, so, bad news first, and it's pretty bad.
Two days ago we found out we don't have new tires for this weekend.
Mo, you want to explain?
Yeah, so for the last two seasons our biggest sponsor has been Hendricks Tire and Auto, the garage down on Mill Street.
Old man Hendricks basically gave us a fresh set of slicks every race weekend, and in return we put his name on the side pods.
And he just sold the business, and the new owners told us on Thursday they're not doing the racing thing anymore.
Which, I get it, it's their money, but losing a sponsor two days before a race is rough.
We're going to have to peel his stickers off at some point, which honestly feels kind of sad.
So we're on the used set from round three, which have, what, maybe two races left in them?
If we're lucky.
Okay, so we're at the track, it's eight in the morning, it's freezing, and Danny is already stressed.
I'm not stressed, I'm focused.
He's stressed.
The plan for practice is to go easy, save the tires, and just get a feel for the grip.
Mo's dropped the pressures a little to try and get more heat into the rubber.
First practice, here we go.
Danny's coming past now, look at the rear stepping out at turn two.
That's the old tires, there's just not the grip there was a month ago.
Okay, he's in, let's see what he thinks.
It's sliding everywhere, the rear is just gone in the slow corners, but the fast stuff is actually okay.
So Mo's going to stiffen the rear a bit and see if that calms it down.
And now, oh no, is that rain?
It's rain, it's actually raining.
Okay, this might be the best thing that could happen to us, because in the wet, everyone's on the same rain tires.
Our old slicks don't matter if nobody's on slicks.
Qualifying, wet track, twenty one karts.
Danny's out early, which is smart, before the line gets too slippery.
He's quick, he's really quick in sector one, he's braking so late into the hairpin.
Come on, come on.
Fourth, he's fourth, that is his best qualifying all season.
In the rain, on the worst week we've had, that's amazing.
Okay, the rain has stopped, and the track's drying for the final, which is not what we wanted.
Everyone's switching back to slicks, so we're back on the old set.
The goal now is honestly just hold position as long as we can.
Lights out, and Danny gets a decent start, he's holding fourth into turn one.
Lap five, he's still fourth, but the kart behind is right on his bumper.
And he's through, the guy just went straight past on the back straight, that's grip, that's just grip.
Lap ten, he's fifth, he's hanging on, the tires are going but he's driving so smart.
Last lap.
Fifth, he finishes fifth.
That's points, on bald tires, in a drying race, I'm so proud of this guy.
So, that's the weekend, we'll figure out the tire situation before round six, somehow.
Thanks for hanging out with us, see you at the next one.
